title: Rama
hook: why would God come as a person, and wait at a shore?
tomorrow: the throne of Ayodhya has no king on it. so what's sitting there?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Parashurama met Rama on the road, saw Vishnu in him, and stepped aside to keep teaching. Today, Rama himself, as the Puranas tell him.

Anyone can post advice. It lands differently when you watch someone live it. Rama stands at the edge of the sea. Sita is on the far side, in Lanka, and between them there's only water. So he asks the ocean to make a way, and waits. Nothing. He waits longer. At last he raises his bow, and the ocean itself rises out of the waves and offers a way across. The question under the scene: why would God come as a person at all?
screen: `WATCH SOMEONE LIVE IT.` → `RAMA ASKS THE SEA, AND WAITS.` → `WHY COME AS A PERSON?`

segments.voice: The Bhagavata Purana gives an answer in Hanuman's words. The Lord came as a human being, he says, to teach human beings. That's the key to the Puranas' Rama. Vishnu as the boar lifts the earth from the waters. Vishnu as Rama waits at a shore, asks first, loses his patience, keeps his promises, grieves, misses his wife. He does what a person does, so people can watch how it's done. Here's one place a neighbor says something close. Christians read in the Gospel of John: “And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us.” Later in the same Gospel, after Jesus washes his friends' feet, he says: “For I have given you an example, that ye should do as I have done to you.” Two traditions, each saying God came close enough to be watched, and copied. And an honest difference. Christians hold that God became human once, in Jesus, and that his life, death and rising save the world. The Puranas tell of Vishnu coming down again and again, in many forms, age after age, Rama among them. Neither account needs the other's to mean what it means. So when the ocean finally rises for Rama, it isn't only a god's power on show. It's a man who asked first.
screen: `A HUMAN, TO TEACH HUMANS.` · `HE ASKS, WAITS, GRIEVES.` · `THE WORD WAS MADE FLESH.` · `ONCE, OR AGE AFTER AGE.` · then, large: `A MAN WHO ASKED FIRST.`

segments.voice: Listen to your own breath coming in and going out, like small waves at a shore. Let each wave arrive in its own time, without pulling it in or pushing it out. If you pray, you can wait there, the way Rama waited at the water.
Rama: in the Puranas, Vishnu come as a human being, to teach human beings how a life is lived.
Keep this one: Rama, the god who asked the ocean first, and then waited. Back tomorrow.

howItsDone: Rama's name is sung in homes and temples, and his birth is celebrated at Rama Navami; the Bhagavata's short telling of his life is read alongside the longer Ramayanas.
